title: Enterprise AI Knowledge Assistant: System Architecture
description: Architect an enterprise-grade AI knowledge platform combining .NET 9 Clean Architecture, .NET Aspire orchestration, React 19 frontend, semantic hybrid search, resilient agent pipelines, and event-driven document ingestion.

data.text: The Capstone project represents the culmination of this curriculum: building an enterprise-grade, secure, multi-tenant AI Knowledge Assistant and Workflow Agent named 'EnterpriseNexus'. Unlike toy chatbot applications, an enterprise AI assistant must deliver sub-second token streaming, resilient failover across multiple LLM providers, granular document-level access control (ACLs), durable multi-step agent execution, and comprehensive OpenTelemetry tracing across all AI interactions.

data.text: To guarantee maintainability, testability, and technology independence, the solution strictly enforces Clean Architecture boundaries. Core business rules (domain entities, value objects, evaluation thresholds) have zero external dependencies. External abstractions like LLM providers, vector databases, and message brokers are isolated behind domain interfaces.

data.caption: EnterpriseNexus Layer Responsibilities & Dependencies
rows: Core Entities (ConversationSession, Message, Citation, DocumentChunk), Domain Events, Enums, Value Objects
CQRS Commands/Queries (MediatR), Pipeline Behaviors (Validation, Logging, Metering), IChatClient Abstractions
Azure OpenAI clients, Azure AI Search vector store, EF Core DbContext, Redis semantic cache, Blob storage
Application, Domain, external SDKs (Azure, Semantic Kernel)
Minimal API route definitions, Server-Sent Events (SSE) endpoints, Entra ID JWT verification, Rate limiting
Application, Infrastructure (for DI composition root only)
.NET Aspire orchestration, container definitions, local dev environment wiring, telemetry dashboard

data.text: .NET Aspire serves as the local development and cloud orchestration backbone. It seamlessly provisions databases, caches, and AI mocks, while injecting connection strings and OpenTelemetry collectors automatically into all services.

data.title: EnterpriseNexus.AppHost Program.cs
data.content: This Aspire definition configures Redis, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Azure OpenAI endpoints, the backend API, the ingestion worker, and the React frontend.

data.title: Architectural Decision: Modular Monolith vs Distributed Microservices
data.content: For this enterprise AI assistant, a modular monolith with in-process message dispatch (using MediatR and System.Threading.Channels) is chosen for the primary query path, paired with an asynchronous background worker for document ingestion. This avoids distributed transaction complexities and network hop latency during token-critical LLM streaming while keeping clear component boundaries for future extraction.

data.title: System Architecture Readiness Checklist
items: Zero circular dependencies between Clean Architecture layers verified via ArchUnitNET or Roslyn analyzers
Streaming endpoints configured with HTTP/2 and Server-Sent Events (SSE) to prevent response buffering
Distributed tracing enabled across frontend, backend API, and AI provider calls using W3C TraceContext
Multi-tenant data isolation enforced at the database and vector index level with partition keys
Circuit breakers and bulkhead isolation configured for all external LLM provider calls
Graceful shutdown handlers configured on background workers to avoid terminating in-flight document embeddings

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: EnterpriseNexus integrates .NET 9 Clean Architecture, .NET Aspire, and React 19.
Clear layer separation isolates LLM and vector database dependencies behind domain abstractions.
.NET Aspire standardizes local orchestrations, telemetry, and container lifecycle.
Next, we define the relational and vector data schemas to support multi-tenant conversations and embeddings.
data.takeaway: A resilient architecture treats AI models as unreliable external network dependencies, surrounding them with clean abstractions, circuit breakers, and comprehensive telemetry.
